description: Purpose: establish the portfolio architectural runway and NFR backbone. Act: Demand. Orchestrator: Value Management Officer. In-scope mains: architecture-vision. Challenges: security (NFR backbone), operability (not evaluated). Evaluate: architecture-vision; KO reiterates the EA owner step. Use when: portfolio NFR backbone, target ARTs, enabler Epic seeds, Architectural Vision itself. Refuse ART ADRs (architectural-runway-extension). Refuse Epic hypothesis (epic-lean-business-case). Strategic Portfolio Review may confirm this main during Cadence; it does not replace this practice.

steps.description: Main artifact draft — Enterprise Architect authors the Architectural Vision and NFR backbone.
Challenge packet — Security Expert security-review of the portfolio NFR backbone. Not itself challenged.
Challenge packet — Operator operability-review of the Architectural Vision. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — Enterprise Architect commits Architectural Vision after the challenge packets.

description: Purpose: write a portfolio bet. Act: Demand. Orchestrator: Value Management Officer. In-scope mains the intent requires: epic, lean-business-case, epic-enabler (sibling, not a review; catalog still walks; out-of-scope siblings get explicit-none). Challenge: Developer feasibility-review (not evaluated). Evaluate: those mains; KO reiterates that main's owner step. Use when: new bet, thicken Epic/LBC, portfolio-sized impact, kill/pivot as a rewrite of that Epic. Do not use for Feature/Story grain (Refuse).

steps.description: Main artifact draft — Business Owner authors the business Epic hypothesis.
Main artifact draft — Business Owner authors the Lean Business Case after discovery.
Main artifact draft — Enterprise Architect sibling Enabler Epic (technical counter-proposal, not a review packet).
Challenge packet — Developer feasibility-review of the Lean Business Case and Enabler Epic. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — Business Owner commits the Lean Business Case after the feasibility challenge.

description: Purpose: cadence snapshot of portfolio risks, WIP, Kanban. Act: Cadence or Inspect. Orchestrator: Value Management Officer. Dispatch: portfolio-sync mediation record. Manifests and Kanban are projections, not mains. Evaluate: nothing as a bet. An impediment that is Epic-sized is a later Demand, not this workflow writing an Epic. Do not Evaluate the minutes.

steps.description: Mediation record — Value Management Officer records the Portfolio Sync. Not itself challenged.
Operational projection — Value Management Officer updates the portfolio manifest from the sync.
Operational projection — Value Management Officer updates product manifests from the sync.
Operational projection — Value Management Officer refreshes Portfolio Kanban from Epic frontmatter.

description: Purpose: allocate or guardrail value-stream / ART funding. Act: Cadence (or Evaluate of the last allocation). Orchestrator: Value Management Officer. Dispatch: budget-allocation. Challenge: Developer feasibility-review (not evaluated). Evaluate: the allocation only. Not Demand — do not mint an Epic. Use when: funding shift, guardrail change. Do not use for a new bet (Demand epic-lean-business-case).

steps.description: Main artifact draft — Business Owner proposes the value-stream / ART budget allocation.
Challenge packet — Developer feasibility-review of the draft allocation. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — Business Owner commits the allocation after the feasibility challenge.

description: Purpose: keep, pivot, stop, or re-rank portfolio bets. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Value Management Officer. Dispatch mains: strategic-themes, portfolio-vision, portfolio-roadmap, architecture-vision (EA sibling main). portfolio-review-decision is mediation, not a main and not evaluated. Evaluate: the four mains. Not Demand — kill/pivot of one Epic as a rewrite is epic-lean-business-case Demand.

steps.description: Main artifact rewrite — Business Owner re-ranks Strategic Themes.
Main artifact rewrite — Business Owner updates Portfolio Vision after the theme rerank.
Main artifact rewrite — Business Owner updates Portfolio Roadmap after the vision rewrite.
Main artifact challenge-as-sibling — Enterprise Architect restates Architecture Vision against the new Portfolio Vision.
Mediation record — Business Owner records the kill/pivot/continue decision. Not itself challenged.

description: Purpose: extend ART architectural runway. Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. In-scope mains: nfr-list, adr, architecture-runway. nfr-list is the product singleton at products/<product-slug>/nfr-list.md, not a Feature-folder file. It is a precondition for ADR production. Same workflow for ADR needed, new or changed product NFR, runway gap, structurant architecture. Challenges of that packet: security, operability, feasibility (not evaluated). Evaluate: those mains; KO reiterates that main's owner step. Late-seeded Enabler Feature forces Feature refinement replay before the Architecture Gate is restaged. Refuse Feature AC/WSJF shaping (that is feature-backlog-refinement). Refuse portfolio NFR backbone (that is architectural-vision). PI Planning only confirms runway; it does not author it.

steps.description: Main artifact draft — System Architect records the NFR list before any ADR.
Main artifact draft — System Architect records one ADR after the NFR list exists.
Challenge packet — Security Expert security-review of the NFR/ADR packet. Not itself challenged.
Challenge packet — Operator operability-review of the NFR/ADR packet. Not itself challenged.
Challenge packet — Developer feasibility-review of the NFR/ADR packet. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — System Architect commits Architecture Runway after the three challenge packets.

description: Purpose: mid-PI inspect of dependencies and impediments. Act: Cadence or Inspect. Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. Dispatch: art-sync mediation record. Kanban and ART manifest are projections. Evaluate: nothing as product. A Feature-sized impediment is a later Demand, not this workflow writing a Feature. Do not Evaluate the minutes.

steps.description: Mediation record — Release Train Engineer records the ART Sync. Not itself challenged.
Operational projection — Release Train Engineer refreshes Program Kanban from the sync.
Operational projection — Release Train Engineer updates the ART manifest from the sync.

description: Purpose: write a PI-ready Feature. Act: Demand. Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. In-scope mains: feature, feature-enabler. Same workflow for new Feature, thicken AC/WSJF, Feature-sized impact of changing X, Feature-sized UX/security gap, Enabler Feature sibling. Challenges of those mains: feasibility, architecture-review (SA challenge, not an ADR), security, UX. Evaluate: those mains; KO reiterates that main's owner step. Refuse Epic/Story grain. Refuse ADR, NFR list, and runway — those are architectural-runway-extension. Do not invent Impact Analysis.

steps.description: Main artifact draft — Product Manager authors the business Feature.
Main artifact draft — System Architect sibling Enabler Feature (not a review packet).
Challenge packet — Developer feasibility-review. Not itself challenged.
Challenge packet — System Architect architecture-review of the Feature/Enabler. Not an ADR.
Challenge packet — Security Expert security-review. Not itself challenged.
Challenge packet — UX Designer ux-review. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — Product Manager commits the Feature after the four challenge packets.
Owner rewrite — System Architect commits the Enabler Feature after the challenge packets.

description: Purpose: split an approved Epic into ART Features (SAFe: Portfolio Epics split into Features on the ART backlog). Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. In-scope mains: feature, feature-enabler. Product Manager derives the business Feature; System Architect derives the Enabler Feature. No challenge protocol here — derived items then enter feature-backlog-refinement. Evaluate: those mains. Refuse Feature AC/WSJF thickening and NFR traces (that is refinement). Refuse ADR/NFR register (that is architectural-runway-extension). There is no Feature-to-Story derivation workflow; teams split Features into Stories in team-backlog-refinement.

steps.description: Main artifact draft — Product Manager derives a business Feature from the approved Epic.
Main artifact draft — System Architect derives the sibling Enabler Feature from the approved Epic.

description: Purpose: PI quantitative/qualitative improve. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. Dispatch: pain-point mediation records. Do not Evaluate pain-points. A resulting Feature or Enabler is a later Demand (feature-backlog-refinement), not I&A writing a Feature.

steps.description: Mediation record — Release Train Engineer records quantitative/qualitative pain-points. Not itself challenged.
Mediation record — Release Train Engineer records retrospective pain-points. Not itself challenged.

description: Purpose: ART commit for the PI. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. Dispatch: confirm product-vision, product-roadmap, feature intent, architecture-runway; write objectives. Challenge: Developer feasibility-review of drafted Objectives (not evaluated). risks is ROAM mediation, not a main. Evaluate: objectives (and a confirmed main only if the user KOs that intent). "I want SSO" here is Refuse — Demand feature-backlog-refinement first.

steps.description: Main artifact confirm — Product Manager restates product vision for this PI.
Main artifact confirm — Product Manager restates the product roadmap for this PI.
Main artifact confirm — Product Manager restates Feature intent that this PI will commit against.
Main artifact confirm — System Architect restates Architecture Runway capacity for this PI.
Main artifact draft — Release Train Engineer proposes committed and stretch PI Objectives.
Challenge packet — Developer feasibility-review of the drafted PI Objectives. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — Release Train Engineer commits PI Objectives after the feasibility challenge.
Mediation ledger — Product Manager records ROAM risks. Not a main artifact; not challenged.

description: Purpose: ship an accepted increment off-cadence. Act: Advance. Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. Dispatch: release-on-demand after Operator operability-review (not evaluated). Evaluate: the release decision. Refuse: "fix prod" with no Story — SM Demand first. Not Demand — do not mint a Feature.

steps.description: Challenge packet — Operator operability-review of Continuous Deployment readiness. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — Product Manager commits the release-on-demand decision after the operability challenge.

description: Purpose: inspect the integrated increment; human demo gate. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Release Train Engineer. Dispatch: system-demo mediation / gate record. Evaluate: the increment shown (Stories/Features), not the minutes.

steps.description: Mediation record — Release Train Engineer records the System Demo / demo gate. Not itself challenged.

description: Purpose: commit the iteration. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Scrum Master. Dispatch: confirm team-manifest; write plan. Challenge: Developer feasibility-review of the drafted plan (not evaluated). Evaluate: the plan. Not Demand — a new bug or Story is team-backlog-refinement.

steps.description: Main artifact confirm — Scrum Master restates team capacity and membership for this iteration.
Main artifact draft — Scrum Master proposes Iteration Goals and the selected Story list.
Challenge packet — Developer feasibility-review of the drafted Iteration Plan. Not itself challenged.
Owner rewrite — Scrum Master commits the Iteration Plan after the feasibility challenge.

description: Purpose: team qualitative improve. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Scrum Master. Dispatch: iteration-retrospective mediation record. Evaluate: nothing as a Story. A resulting Story is a later Demand. Do not Evaluate minutes.

steps.description: Mediation record — Scrum Master records the Iteration Retrospective. Not itself challenged.

description: Purpose: inspect the increment at iteration end. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Scrum Master. Dispatch: iteration-review mediation record. Evaluate: the increment shown, not the minutes.

steps.description: Mediation record — Scrum Master records the Iteration Review. Not itself challenged.

description: Purpose: implement an already-OK Story. Act: Advance. Orchestrator: Scrum Master. Dispatch: code-change (driver). Navigator authors no second artifact. Built-In Quality of the code is verification qa-signoff, not an in-pair packet. Evaluate: not the code-change as a Demand; "this isn't what I meant" is KO of the Story (Demand rewrite) or stay in Advance. Not Demand — do not mint a Story.

steps.description: Main artifact — Developer records the pair-programming code-change. Challenged later by verification, not by a navigator packet.

description: Purpose: write a ready-enough Story, including splitting a Feature into Stories (SAFe: teams split Features into Stories; there is no named Story-derivation ceremony). Orchestrator: Scrum Master. In-scope mains: story, story-enabler. Same workflow for new Story, bug, spike, debt slice, thicken AC, split. Challenges of those mains: feasibility, UX, architecture-review (SA challenge, not an ADR). Evaluate: those mains; KO reiterates that main's owner step. Refuse Feature/Epic grain. Refuse ADR and the product NFR register (hand off to RTE architectural-runway-extension). Stories inherit NFR applicability from the parent Feature; they do not define NFRs. Do not invent Bug Intake.

steps.description: Main artifact draft — Product Owner authors the business Story.
Main artifact draft — System Architect sibling Enabler Story (not a review packet).
Challenge packet — Developer feasibility-review of the Story and Enabler Story. Not itself challenged.
Challenge packet — UX Designer ux-review of the Story. Not itself challenged.
Challenge packet — System Architect architecture-review of the Story. Not an ADR.
Owner rewrite — Product Owner commits the Story after the challenge packets.

description: Purpose: daily inspect-and-adapt of the iteration. Act: Cadence. Orchestrator: Scrum Master. Dispatch: team-sync mediation record. Evaluate: nothing as a Story. Fallout Demand goes to team-backlog-refinement. Do not Evaluate minutes.

steps.description: Mediation record — Scrum Master records the Team Sync. Not itself challenged.

description: Purpose: is this Story done. Act: Advance. Orchestrator: Scrum Master. Dispatch: qa-signoff, which IS the challenge of Story and code-change. Do not Evaluate the signoff. Evaluate: Story done-ness. Security is not a second verification actor. Not Demand.

steps.description: Challenge packet — Quality Engineer qa-signoff of the Story / code-change. Not itself challenged.
